//: Configuration for the JavaScript language server ONLY (typescript-lsp plugin, and VS Code's
built-in JS intelligence). This project ships no TypeScript and does not compile: nothing here
affects runtime, tests, or the build. It exists so go-to-definition and find-references resolve
ESM imports correctly instead of guessing.
package.json declares "type": "module" and every import carries an explicit .js extension
(Node ESM requires it), so the server must be told to resolve the same way Node does — the
default 'classic'/bundler resolution silently fails on './foo.js' style specifiers and produces
'cannot find module' noise on correct code.
checkJs is deliberately OFF. Turning it on would flood 177 untyped JS files with implicit-any
and property-does-not-exist errors, and this project's correctness bar is its 2,700-test suite,
not a type checker retrofitted after the fact. Navigation is the goal here, not type enforcement.
